name: 17484-gsm8kbatch-llada2mini-1gpu
model: inclusionAI/LLaDA2.0-mini, bf16. Not substitutable: the engine's diffusion-LLM path serves only LLaDA2MoeModelLM, and the one sibling checkpoint (LLaDA2.0-flash) is ~103B and does not fit one card.
hardware: 1x H100 80GB HBM3 of one a3 node (--gres=gpu:1). ~32.5 GiB of weights on an 80 GB card leaves ample room at mem-fraction-static 0.9. No router, no external cache tier.
parallelism: TP=1, PP=1, DP=1, no expert parallelism. One GPU, one node. Pipeline parallelism is force-disabled by the engine under --dllm-algorithm regardless.
architecture: LLaDA2MoeModelLM, 16.3B parameters (~32.5 GiB bf16 over 7 shards), ~1.4B active per token, 256 experts at top-8, 20 layers. A diffusion LM: it generates in blocks of 32, not one token per forward. Ungated on the hub.
load_profile: concurrent (closed loop), streams=32, warmup the first 20%, bounded at 400 requests with an 1800 s safety cap. Streams has a floor -- see load_note.
workload: guidellm `json_file` over configs/data/gsm8k-5shot-200.jsonl -- 200 single-turn five-shot GSM8K prompts built from the test split (openai/gsm8k, config main) the way the engine's own in-tree evaluation harness builds them, five `Question: ...\nAnswer: ...` pairs as a shared preamble and then the row being asked. Against this checkpoint's tokenizer that is 865.8 prompt tokens on average (sd 23.9, min 829, max 939), of which the shared preamble is 800. Each request generates exactly 128 tokens under `ignore_eos: true` at `temperature: 0.0` -- four whole 32-token blocks, none partial. 400 requests over 200 prompts is two passes; the engine force-disables its prefix cache under --dllm-algorithm, so the second pass gets no reuse the first did not. Seed 17484.
purpose: A 16B diffusion language model tutoring grade-school math from five-shot prompts, 128-token answers, four concurrent users, one GPU.
launch:
model-path: inclusionAI/LLaDA2.0-mini

# The checkpoint ships configuration_llada2_moe.py / modeling_llada2_moe.py; without this
# the architecture does not resolve and the server refuses to start.
trust-remote-code: true

tp-size: 1
mem-fraction-static: 0.9

# LOAD-BEARING. The dLLM path reads its own admission limit off this argument and DEFAULTS
# IT TO 1 when it is absent -- an unset flag means one request at a time, silently, not
# "unlimited". This setup is about serving four at once.
max-running-requests: 4

# Forced by the engine on CUDA whenever cuda graphs are on under --dllm-algorithm; written
# down explicitly rather than left to the engine to infer.
attention-backend: flashinfer

dllm-algorithm: LowConfidence

# Every integer up to max-running-requests. The dLLM batch size varies round to round, and
# an uncaptured size falls back to the eager path, which is unusually expensive here (the
# unmasking loop does several host syncs per request per step).
cuda-graph-bs: [1, 2, 3, 4]
